steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Baroque music features basso continuo (keyboard + cello/bass providing harmonic foundation) and terraced dynamics (sudden dynamic shifts, not gradual).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Handel's Coronation Anthems exemplify Baroque grandeur: choral polyphony, orchestral doubling, majestic key choices and ceremonial character.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ground bass (repeated bass pattern) provides structural foundation — used in arias and instrumental works by Purcell and Handel.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ornamentation (trills, mordents, grace notes) was often improvised by performers — Baroque notation is simpler than what was actually played.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how baroque music 1650-1750 are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative languag | A practical application showing understanding of how baroque music 1650-1750 can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
